products.name: Soundcore by Anker Q20i Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Black
products.description: Hybrid ANC with feedforward and feedback mics neutralizes a wider range of noise. Settle into a quieter space around you. Use the soundcore app to tailor noise cancellation to your environment. (ANC/Normal/Transparency) Flexible headband and 90° rotating ear cups for custom fit. 40mm dynamic drivers produce detailed sound, from the deeper bass to the higher treble. Gain a decisive tactical advantage with expertly-tuned sound. Enjoy up to 60-hour playback and a rapid 5-min charge for when you're in a rush. Voice-isolating technology filters out background noise for clear calls. Automatically switch from your conference to an incoming phone call. Is there a noise cancelling feature in AUX-in state? No, the AUX-in state does not feature noise cancelling. ANC works in Bluetooth mode only - it pauses automatically in wired mode. How should I use ANC mode for a better experience? 1. Check whether you are wearing the headphones correctly and whether the left and right are reversed; 2. Ensuire the earpads completely cover your ears; 3. Adjust the length of the headphones to ensure it fits correctly. How can I adjust the audio settings If the default sound isn’t for me? The Soundcore app (iOS & Android) offers multiple EQ presets as well as manual tuning, allowing you to adjust the sound profile—such as bass, mids, and treble—to better suit your listening preferences. How do I reconnect my soundcore Q20i headphones? Press and hold the "Power On" button for 3s until you hear the boot up tone, and the headphones will automatically reconnect to the last device. If not, after continuously sending a reconnection signal for 5s, it will enter into pairing mode again. How can I get the most comfortable fit from my Q20i? The Q20i's memory foam ear cushions soften and adapt to your head shape within the first few days of use. Start with the headband at mid-length for optimal fit. To accelerate the process, gently flex the headband over a stack of books overnight.

reviews.text: I don’t write reviews as often as I should, unless a product is something to rave about. I live in an apartment. For some reason after six years of living here, the loudest person in the city has moved in above me. The noise cancellation on these headphones is phenomenal. I don’t even have to turn any music on. Just dead silence. Peace. And when I do turn music on the sound is so crisp and perfect I get lost in my own world. I have so many Apple products. My son has the beats. But these. .. for the price I just can’t believe what a steal this is. And I like listening to loud music. Trust me if that’s what you’re looking for that’s what you will get lol This product is by far absolutely worth this long review. So much so I think I may just buy a back up here. They are so durable they are so comfortable. They are built so well I love the color in my 39 years. I’ve never been happier with a pair of headphones. They stay charged forever. They don’t take long to charge. They’re so easy to connect. Just buy them.

reviews.title: Phenomenal. Absolutely amazed.

reviews.text: These Sound ore by Anker Q20i headphones are absolutely amazing. I am an earbud girlie all the way, but let’s be real, the noise cancelling effect is only in play when you’re playing music on your ears buds. In the other hand, these headphones, as soon as they just connect to any of my devices, provide the noise cancelling effect I was looking for! I wanted noise cancelling headphones to block out the noise of home - I have 3 kids that always have some sort of device and my fiancé who ALWAYS has the tv on and loud. I love that I can pop these on if if I’m not playing anything through them at the moment. - I also love the fact that they can be connected/paired to multiple devices. They are currently paired to my phone, iPad, and switch lite. I use these a lot to play music through my phone or while gaming on my switch lite. BONUS- you can simultaneously have these connected to 2 devices at once. Using them while gaming but also connected to my phone so I won’t miss an important phone call. The headphones do have specific sides R/L that are marked accordingly. If you out them on backwards, they still work BUT if you are trying to use the mic, it will drastically impact the ability for the other person to hear you- so just make sure you put them on the right way. - most headphones are EXTREMELY big on my head as I do have a smaller head- others would fall off the back of my head if I tilted it backwards or fly off the front when I sat up. These do not do that! Do they move some? Yes, but they are by far the best fitting headphones I have ever tried. -also, I have never been able to wear headphones around my neck because they always make me feel like I’m choking, these however don’t and are the first ones I have ever been able to wear around my neck when needing to pause use for a time. - The ear pads/pillows are SO comfortable, they literally feel like little pillow clouds on my ears. They are comfortable enough to lay down with while wearing and I mean laying on my side too. - the sound is incredible, the volume control is top notch! You can turn the volume up all the way if you like, but it’s really not necessary, and I have hearing loss on both sides. (See screenshot showing my perfect volume level with these) - There is an app you can download and adjust your equalizer to personalize it. I just use the Bass booster setting. - the battery life is amazing- far superior to my earbuds. I have only charged them once since I bought them yet and I have had them for nearly 2 weeks now. - these are actually my second pair as the first ones the band seemed as though it had been stretched out and had a pin hole in the ear pad. They replaced them super quick without issue. - they are very durable as previously stated with me sleeping on them. Initially I just tossed them into my bag, but I wanted to protect my investment (I normally don’t really spend money on myself) so I was even able to get a case for these! - oh, I almost forgot! I love how you can fold these too for storage! Makes it super nice for sure! If you’re in doubt, take the jump- I promise you won’t regret your purchase with these!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on March 20, 2026
reviews.title: Best headphones ever! You won’t regret these bad boys!

reviews.text: These headphones are awesome!! I am someone who is extremely sensitive to sound so having noise cancelling headphones is an absolute must! I've owned quite a few pairs and all have worked fine. I actually bought these for my husband but have been using them myself. Without spending $$$ these headphones really give top dollar quality. They are exceptionally comfortable (no ear pain after long use), have really great sound quality and the noise cancelling is phenomenal (true noise cancelling). The headphones come with different adjustments so you are able to turn off the noise cancelling effect and use as typical over-ear headphones (allowing outside noises in). The headphones also have a microphone feature and allow you to talk through them. My husband uses them for work calls and meetings all the time. The headphones charge fairly quickly and have a long lasting charge once at full capacity. Easy to connect to devices with the ability to connect to multiple devices at once. The headphones are comfortable and fit myself, my husband and even our elementary age daughter (although a little big on her, of course). The headphones fold up and become fairly compact and easy to store on-the-go. My husband's one complaint is that there is a sort of ear discomfort if wearing the headphones while on the noise cancelling feature is on without listening to anything. He said the reverse sound effect will start to really bother his ears after a while if he forgets to play music or turn the feature off. My one complaint is that I haven't bought a pair for myself yet! We love these and would definitely recommend! 10/10

reviews.title: Great noise cancelling headphones! Truly.

reviews.text: The title of the review sets the stage and helps to understand where I'm coming from when I purchased the Soundcore by Anker Q20i headphones. BACKSTORY A few years ago I had purchased a pair of Apple AirPods Max, which are probably the best pair of headphones I've ever owned: amazing sound quality, awesome noise cancellation, and unreal support for Transparency Mode. However due to Apple's dubious quality of engineering on that product, they begin to fail after what I consider be too short a time. When they died this last time, I began looking for cheaper alternatives. The obvious one is the Beats Studio Pro, which are actually priced very well for a decent pair of headphones. Instead, I wanted to get something that was a cheaper stopgap, so I started exploring the over-the-ear Soundcore headphones by Anker, because I had had decent experience with them in the past with their Bluetooth earbuds and also approximately 10 years ago I had one of the successor models to the Q20i. So I thought I would give it a shot. I purchased a different pair of Soundcore headphones at first, but when they arrived they had an offensive smell and had to send them back. After that experience, I do not know what motivated me to try the Soundcore Q20i model, but immediately on arrival I had a different experience. There was no offensive smell, the headphones are very comfortable on my (admittedly large) head. SOUND QUALITY As far as sound quality is concerned, they are passable-to-pretty-good. They initially sounded a little "tinny", but I typically run them with the bass boost and I think I've gotten used to the way that they sound at this point. My typical use case is wearing my headphones pretty much all day listening to droning ambient electronic music so I can focus while working. Therefore, I am not necessarily looking for stellar audio quality, but these are actually pretty good for the price. One cannot compare them to the AirPods Max, because those headphones just blew me away by their quality. But given that this is a $45 pair of headphones, the sound is great—for the price. (I will keep saying that just to keep perspective: "For the price…") TRANSPARENCY MODE The other reason why I went for these is because I needed a pair of headphones that had Transparency Mode, but I didn't have the extra cash to spend on the Beats Studio Pro. The Q20i surprised me because it has a Transparency Mode in a $45 pair of headphones. It's important to acknowledge that Transparency Mode on the Q20i is *nowhere near* the same experience of Transparency Mode on AirPods Max or AirPods Pro, so don't expect that level. However, it does let in enough ambient sound to allow me to hear sound around me and to have a conversation with someone without having to take the headphones off. That was the crucial feature requirement. So again, for the price, having Transparency Mode at all is pretty amazing. STAR REMOVAL The only reason I took off a star is because I feel that the headphones should have the capacity to remember that I always want to have transparency on, or at least remember the last setting of that mode so that when I turned them on the next time, it will be in the same mode that I left it. These do not do that, and for that, I docked a star. OTHER TOPICS Battery life has been good, but I work at a desk and I can charge them whenever I need to, so I am probably not the best judge of that. The headphones are light and comfortable, and they are very adjustable so they should be able to fit and be comfortable for most wearers. They also fold for easy transportation and seem like a pretty durable construction. CONCLUSION For a sub $50 pair of headphones that has transparency mode, has reasonably good sound quality, and so far has been behaving decently on the Bluetooth side connected to a MacBook Pro, I definitely recommend them to someone who is on a tight budget, or someone who just wants a "burner" set of Bluetooth over the ear headphones.

reviews.title: For The Price, These Headphones are Amazing

reviews.text: I’ve had the cream colored headphones for about a year and loved them so much, I got the black ones for my daughter. The active noise cancellation is excellent, which was the main thing I was looking for. I like to listen to audiobooks while doing loud things like power washing, woodworking, running the leaf blower. I did kind of cover them in wood stain when I was painting a fence with an airless sprayer, but they even cleaned up pretty well. I’ve never managed to run the batteries down, and can go a week or so between charges, although often I just plug them in instead of turning them off. The audio quality seems good (no interruptions while listening) and I’ve taken calls while out walking and it worked well for that (remote caller could hear me over the mic with no complaints). My main complaint is that they are HOT to wear, your ears will definitely get sweaty. Also, they’re pretty big. They tend to fall forward on my head even on the smallest setting. Even so, I love them and definitely recommend!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 28, 2026
reviews.title: Excellent Value

reviews.text: My 13yo son ordered these headphones and he says he likes them - they’re comfortable, the noise cancelling works well, and they easily paired with multiple devices (phone, Alexa, Kindle, computer). The battery life says something like 40 hours, he’s had them for a week and hasn’t had to charge them yet. They get plenty loud, but my teen finds that with the noise cancelling he doesn’t need the volume up too high. He can hear that I’m talking to him but not what I’m saying, but I’m able to get his attention easily. The volume buttons in the side are easy to find and use. He likes that there is an aux cord and he can use them with non-Bluetooth devices or if the battery dies. They don’t come with a case so we recommend ordering a hard case, we ordered the L LTGEM case and it works well. The headphones are a little finicky to fold up into the case but we took a look at the listing pictures and figured it out. It looks like the ear pads are replaceable, which further extends the life of your headphones. I’ll be honest - they’re not as nice as my Bose QuietComfort headphones, but for the price these Anker headphones are a great option, especially for kids.

reviews.title: Good sound quality, easy to pair, comfortable, NO CASE!

reviews.text: I really have been liking these headphones quite a bit. I needed something to use with my Android TV device for watching movies late at night. The sound quality is good, the buttons have indentations and features you can feel with your fingers as needed - though I don't fiddle with the controls much since I use my TV remote to adjust volume, pause etc. I have used these to talk on the phone once and the person on the other end could hear me adequately. I really appreciate the fast sync up time after turning on the headphones to whatever you'll be using them with. As some have mentioned, its a little difficult to tell when the headphones are on or have turned on after holding the power button for a second. There is a light but more than once I have held the button too long and put the device into bluetooth pairing mode which was not intended. If you are wearing the headphones there is an audible tone for "on" and "off" which makes operation much easier. The noise cancelling is honestly very good. I have had better on other device (Pixelbuds for example) but these are over the ear design and they are more than adquate for blocking out everyday living room sounds like when the vacuum is running etc. If you're using at a busy airport I'm not sure how good the cancellation would be. I do intend to use them while flying eventually however. Overall I am very happy with the price point and fit and function of these headphones. They are very comfortable to wear even after several hours, although some heat is added to your head, but that is normal for this style. This product resolidified what I already know about Anker and that is that they create high quality products that do not cut corners. Sure the headphones have some tiny weaknesses - but again for the price point I'm very glad I went with a brand name instead of some Temu junk. Anker is a solid name in portable battery packs but apparently they make other high quality products as well. I can attest to that.

reviews.title: High quality, to be expected from Anker - very happy with these headphones.

reviews.text: I bought two sets of NC headphones and the more expensive $80 ones offered none even in NC mode. These are eons better! I also love the color! Even though it says white, it is more like an oatmeal white, very pretty. Next time these go on sale, I plan on buying a back up pair. Pros: Super comfortable from the fit of the ear pieces to the headband. I prefer on ear headphones so over ear, like these, usually aren't comfortable for me, so I was pleasantly surprised. The NC mode works extremely well! As soon as they are on I think it blocks out like 90% of sound before I even play any sound. I have noisy upstairs neighbors who stay between 60-90 decibels loud. So think of a busy, loud restaurant kitchen, that's the base for them above my head. Can't speak to their peak loudness (90 db), but their normal low end (60 db), I didn't hear them thankfully. The volume/loudness is impressive. I have used Jlab neons (they are on ear vs over ear like these) for 5+ years and always had to have my laptop volume up in the high 70 range, usually 77. With these, I majorly had to turn it down to about 44. The sound is really great. I played around with the different modes on the app to get the sound I am used too. So I am thankful for that. I do like the three modes you can easily switch between NC, Normal, and Awareness. I had my mother who has hearing aids try these on and the Awareness mode majorly boosted my voice for her which my vocal range is in the range she has a hard time hearing. I really like that this uses a type C charger. Everything I use requires that so I can just use my phone charger (10ft) if I need to vs searching for a micro usb (I believe) that my old ones used. And these also come with a cord to turn these into a wired version as well. I don't know if you can do that and be able to listen while they charge or not. But if so, even better! My biggest pro is that I can pair these to my laptop (main use) and phone at the same time! This allowed me to keep watching my show while I played with the app on my phone to customize the sound. I just want to mention the color again. A beautiful oatmeal white which makes it more unique. I tend to go for purples and pinks so I went with white just because it was the cheaper option and I am so glad I did! Cons: It automatically reverts to NC mode when you power them on. Not a big deal, but I wish it stayed how I left them when powered off. Button positions. I'm used to buttons on the left earpiece so I am having to relearn/get used to having them on the right. The NC button (which cycles the three modes) is on the opposite side of the same earpiece and is hard to find blindly. I like that it is out of the way so I don't accidentally hit it when powering on/off or volume controls. But I wish it were placed a bit higher so where your finger naturally goes to search for it, it'd find it. My biggest issue, but not enough to knock a star off, are the cues. I'm used to a voice telling me which mode I'm in, power on/off, etc. These ones use a chime that sounds the same for everything, so I have no clue what each chime is telling me until I cycle through enough times or use the app.

reviews.title: Amazing NC headphones!

globalReviews.text: Definitely 5 stars for the price. I am got these to replace my Sony MDR 1000x (basically the old version of the XM4). Which were 5 X more expensive than these. I beat of my headphones, running, using them for the gym, lots of travel and being thrown into bags. So I decided to go for a cheaper option this time. Although my Sony's lasted almost 10 years I had to keep repairing them myself to keep them going. So here's my comparison against a pretty premium pair of headphones- my wife also has Bose QC35's and I've used them plenty too. Pros: - Sound Isolation is amazing, it has a very good seal over the ears (I have a big head and ears too) - Very comfortable, and suprisingly light. Ear cups feel memory foamish - noise cancelling is pretty great, and it doesn't cause discomfort like some cheap NC - Bass is powerful if you like that - they look good and feel of reasonable quality - the battery is as advertised Cons: - Sound quality over all is not spectacular, but good for the price. The bass is good but the mids and highs are a bit muddy. Honestly though it's completely fine and probably the best sound you'll get around this price. - Turning on the Noise cancelling causes a noticeable dip in sound quality. Although the NC is very impressive, it definitely causes the sound quality to become a bit more tinny. While the bass is still there. Everything else gets washed out. I find myself needing to change EQ settings when I turn NC On and Off. For this reason I have been using them with NC off mostly ( a bit annoying too as it defaults to being on everytime) So if you're tossing up between getting these or breaking the bank. Just know the main thing you'll sacrifice is sound quality. The NC is good, the soundcore app is nice enough, they look good and even sound decent enough. I'm perfectly happy to use these instead of more expensive headphones.
globalReviews.title: Great value

globalReviews.text: Couleur : Blanc J’utilise ces écouteurs depuis environ 6 mois et je les adore. Je ne suis pas une spécialiste du son, mais pour une utilisation quotidienne, je les trouve excellents. La qualité audio est vraiment belle, autant pour la musique que pour les vidéos et les balados. La réduction de bruit est impressionnante. Elle aide vraiment à diminuer les bruits autour et permet de mieux profiter de ce qu’on écoute. Je ne pensais pas que ça ferait une aussi grande différence avant de les essayer. La connexion Bluetooth est très fiable. Je peux me déplacer dans la maison, même changer de pièce, sans perdre la connexion. Côté confort, c’est un gros coup de cœur. Les écouteurs sont munis de coussinets très doux et les ouvertures sont assez grandes pour bien envelopper les oreilles. Comme j’ai des oreilles un peu plus grandes, c’est souvent un problème avec certains modèles, mais pas avec ceux-ci. Je peux les porter pendant plusieurs heures sans inconfort. L’autonomie est tout simplement exceptionnelle. Après 6 mois d’utilisation, je n’ai eu à les recharger qu’une seule fois. C’est probablement ce qui me surprend le plus. Ils semblent également robustes et bien fabriqués. Malgré une utilisation régulière, ils sont encore en excellent état. Bref, je suis vraiment satisfaite de mon achat. Entre le confort, la qualité sonore, la réduction de bruit, la portée Bluetooth et l’autonomie incroyable, je trouve qu’ils offrent un excellent rapport qualité-prix. Je les recommande sans hésitation.
globalReviews.title: Un must à avoir sans aucun doute

globalReviews.text: Ich hatte hier zuvor im Rahmen eines Angebotes die Hama Calypso erworben, da ich nur ein günstiges an ihr Headset wollte, um in der Wohnung oder auf dem Balkon auch mal laut Musik hören zu können oder ungestört Serie schauen zu können. Die Akkulaufzeit hat mich da schon sehr beeindruckt aber das Headset war insgesamt sehr knarzig hatte nicht wirklich den beigen Farbton, den ich wollte (eher grau) und nach der Zeit taten die Polster auf den Ohren weh, obwohl sehr weich. Die Hammer haben keinen aktives NoiseCancelling. Dann habe ich dieses Angebot entdeckt im Rahmen der Prime Days und war von den Reviews und den Bewertungen bei YouTube beeindruckt Das Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis schien absolut zu stimmen.. und auch jetzt in der Realität kann ich das bestätigen für den Preis ein Top Headset? Es sieht wirklich schön aus, ist sehr flexibel und angenehm zu tragen. Auch nach mehreren Stunden tun mir die Polster nicht an den Ohren weh. Sie sind wirklich ultra weich und haben eine sehr gute Passform für meine Ohren. Die Bedienung am Headset selbst ist sehr einfach. Innerhalb der App kann man nicht wirklich für einstellen aber es ist okay. Mir selbst reichen für Serie gucken und laut Musik hören bei Hausarbeit und Co. Die voreingestellten SoundSettings. Die drei Stufen beim NC Hab natürlich Auswirkungen auf den Ton, weshalb ich je nach Modus (Serie oder Musik) umstellen muss, damit es sich gut anhört. Das finnisch lässt sich sehr hochwertig an. Und anders als die Hama Calypso knarzen sie nicht. Bin wirklich sehr sehr happy mit diesem Kauf.
globalReviews.title: Tolles Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis

globalReviews.text: Me encantan, son cómodos y ligeros. Apenas cumpliré tres semanas con ellos y no tienen peros. Tienen una app para configurar el tipo de sonido, o si lo deseas tiene ecualizador para que tú mismo hagas tus ajustes de acuerdo a tus gustos. Los bajos están bien presentes, tienen un sonido envolvente y la cancelación de ruido es buena, no tienes una cancelación total, pero la suficiente para que escuches con claridad lo que estás reproduciendo sin tener que subir demasiado el volumen. Y la cancelación de ruido la puedes activar y desactivar directamente desde un botón que se ubica justo en el manos libres de los audífonos, así de fácil. La batería es una joya, desde que los pedí los cargué una sola vez, y tiene dos semanas que no los he cargado y apenas se han descargado al 55% en un uso algo prolongando, de unas 2 a 5 hrs diarias aproximadamente. Valen completamente la pena, por el precio y la calidad que ofrecen en sus materiales y el audio que es hi-rez. Si eres un consumidor estricto y quieres lo mejor en sonido y calidad mejor busca una opción acorde a tus necesidades, éste es un gran producto pero no es gama top y tampoco pretende serlo.
globalReviews.title: Una gran elección

aplusFaqList.question: Is there a noise cancelling feature in AUX-in state?
aplusFaqList.answer: No, the AUX-in state does not feature noise cancelling. ANC works in Bluetooth mode only - it pauses automatically in wired mode.

aplusFaqList.question: How should I use ANC mode for a better experience?
aplusFaqList.answer: 1. Check whether you are wearing the headphones correctly and whether the left and right are reversed;

aplusFaqList.question: How can I adjust the audio settings If the default sound isn’t for me?
aplusFaqList.answer: The Soundcore app (iOS & Android) offers multiple EQ presets as well as manual tuning, allowing you to adjust the sound profile—such as bass, mids, and treble—to better suit your listening preferences.

aplusFaqList.question: How do I reconnect my soundcore Q20i headphones?
aplusFaqList.answer: Press and hold the "Power On" button for 3s until you hear the boot up tone, and the headphones will automatically reconnect to the last device. If not, after continuously sending a reconnection signal for 5s, it will enter into pairing mode again.

aplusFaqList.question: How can I get the most comfortable fit from my Q20i?
aplusFaqList.answer: The Q20i's memory foam ear cushions soften and adapt to your head shape within the first few days of use. Start with the headband at mid-length for optimal fit. To accelerate the process, gently flex the headband over a stack of books overnight.

reviews.text: Uliptz headphones may not be the top brand on the market and I’m certainly not what you would call an audiophile, but the sound quality and comfort is superior to some of the mid and high range headsets in the market for a fraction of the cost. I first took a chance on this brand about 2-3 years ago (I’d have to check amazon to be sure) and I am so glad I did. In fact, the main reason I purchased a second pair is because I though I lost the black pair! These are the most comfortable over-head wireless headphones I own to date. These are also the only pair with the greatest bluetooth range that is stable and works with the samsung ultra since a headphone jack is no longer built in. With the exception of a little swelling on the interior portion of the headband -probably from heat and my hot head when mowing the lawn, the headband and earpads portion appear in like-new condition with no fading, peeling or discoloration, and no change in comfort level. I’m guessing the large oval earcup shape has much to do with the comfort since the feel & cushioning is more natural. I have found them comfortable for long sessions of 6+ hours and after having fallen asleep wearing them on several occasions. The headphones not only survived my tossing and turning through the night without cracks or breaking but my ears had no pressure soreness the next morning! They are definitely durable and work well indoors as well as outdoors. I use the headphones when at home listening to music, watching tv, movies, podcasts etc. I also wear them listening to music when outdoors mowing! Other stuff: - Battery life & charging. Charging takes about 2 hours. I’ve never timed it so can’t say for sure. All I can say is a full charge can last a couple weeks between charges depending on your use (65 hours)!!! - Pairing & Bluetooth. The bluetooth range is reported as 33 feet but I swear the connection on this device allows me to go further than on my other devices which usually is as far as the laundry room before out of range/disconnecting. This pair allows for past the laundry room, onto the back patio, into the yard and almost into the back lot with a connection that is stable and reliable. I can actually mow the lawn leaving my phone in the house. The connection is immediate once pairing is established (“WH2037A”). It works with all bluetooth devices. -Answering Calls & microphone. In all my years of owning the headphones, I never had them on when a call came in until last week. I couldn’t find the phone, so I took a chance and hit the button to take the call and knock-on-wood it wasn’t a telemarketer! My friend came in clear and crisp, and was advised that my voice was likewise, meaning a pretty good microphone is built-in to handle calls. I was able to talk and walk and not lose the connection while searching for my phone. -Noise cancelling. It wasn’t a consideration or deal breaker for me. The headphones are not “noise cancelling” so don’t expect to “tune out” your barking dog or TV. On the other hand, anyone sitting close to you will not be bothered by your music, so I guess it does provide some noise blocking. -Sound Quality. It’s exceptional for the price point! I have found music, vocals and speech to come in clear with a nice balance. They are great for casual listening, and use with non-professional video mixing/editing software projects. The headset comes with 6 EQ modes to deliver a more personal experience. Overall, I am pleased with my purchase. As they say, you get what you pay for. For once, I can honestly say you’re getting a better value for the price which just doesn’t happen much anymore. These are a great price, exceptional value, portable, durable, comfortable, and excellent sound quality for the casual listener at a price that’s hard to beat. 5 stars!

reviews.text: These headphones have been really good for the price. They are very loud and clear but they do struggle with bass, other than that the sound is great. It blocks out surrounding noise really well. People can hear me clearly on phone calls without any problems. I did notice that if I'm already on the phone and I try to connect these Bluetooth headphones to my call I have to disconnect it and reconnect it again before the other person can hear me. It didn't start out like that but if my Bluetooth headphones are already connected before I receive a call it's not a problem at all. The battery life is excellent. I purchased these headphones several weeks ago and still have not needed to charge them, and I'm currently at 50%. I would give these headphones a 98 out of 100, and I would recommend them if you're looking to save money, be comfortable, and be functional. But if you're looking for something with strong clear bass, I would look elsewhere.

globalReviews.text: Tenía mis dudas sobre estos audífonos por el precio, solo 23 dólares y prometían ser una maravilla. Y lo son, me arriesgué y los pedí, vienen con cable tipo C, cable de 3,5 mm y bolsita de tela, ah y un manual ultra resumido que básicamente te dice cómo encenderlos y cómo vincularlos, y eso es todo. Lo del botón para ecualizar ni lo mencionan, tampoco cómo adelantar canciones, pero eso no importa. Lo que me gustó fue lo siguiente: tienen bluetooth 5.2, lo que significa más alcance, mayor velocidad de conexión y menor latencia. En cuanto a la ecualización: en el lado izquierdo traen un botón que otros modelos de audífonos usan para la función de cancelación de ruido, en su lugar, este botón trae grabado "EQ" y en la información del vendedor (por cierto muy completa y atractiva) dice que cuentan con las modalidades "bass", "medium" y "treble", pero los que me llegaron traen 6 diferentes modos: jazz, rock, pop, classic, folk y otro que no entiendo lo que dice porque cada vez que presionas el botón se escucha una voz femenina nombrando estos modos. En lo personal me agradó mucho esta mejora. La calidad de audio en general es buena, para probarlos les puse el cable que incluyen y los comparé con unos Superlux HD668b y unos Sennheiser HD599 los 3 conectados a un mini amplificador y a la mitad del volumen no distorsionan para nada (ninguno de los 3 audífonos se pueden escuchar a más de la mitad del volumen de este mini amplificador sin riesgo de lastimar tus oídos) De los 3, los Uliptz son los que tienen bajos más marcados (obvio que los otros dos audífonos se escuchan mejor en general y son de tipo abierto y los Uliptz son cerrados pero quedé sorprendido con la calidad de audio de estos audífonos tan económicos). Debo señalar que los modos de ecualización no funcionan cuando los Uliptz tienen el cable como fuente de sonido. Los materiales son totalmente de plástico salvo una parte metálica de la diadema que sirve para ajustar a la cabeza (los Sennheiser 599 tienen esa parte de plástico) las copas son de un material muy suave que se siente cómodo y junto con su mínimo peso hace que de verdad te olvides que los traes puestos, de nuevo: algo totalmente inesperado por el bajo precio. En cuanto a la duración de la batería: la publicidad dice que aguantas 65 horas de uso con una sola carga, sí, 65 horas, sin embargo en la caja dice que son "solo" 55 horas, jajaja, en este apartado también cumplen, salidos de la caja, al vincularlos, el smartphone me indicaba que la batería estaba al 90%, después de varios días de uso (unas 15 canciones cada vez) me marca que le batería tiene 80%, una maravilla de rendimiento. Por todo lo anterior es por lo que he evaluado estos Uliptz con 5 estrellas en comodidad, calidad-precio y duración de batería. Compra super recomendada si no pierdes de vista que son audífonos de menos de 25 dólares. Nota para los expertos en audio: claro que este producto es de materiales baratos, claro que hay muchos otros que se escuchan mejor, pero honestamente no se puede pedir más por ese precio, se escuchan como si fueran audífonos de más de 100 dólares.

globalReviews.text: I am absolutely thrilled with this headphone set! From the moment I unboxed them, I knew I had found a gem. The build quality is impressive, especially considering the affordable price. The headphones feel sturdy and comfortable, with plush ear cups that make extended listening sessions a breeze. One of the standout features is the battery life. These headphones can go for many hours before needing a recharge. I've used them for an entire day of work and still had plenty of battery left. They even have an automatic power-off feature, which kicks in after prolonged inactivity to conserve battery life. This thoughtful design element ensures that the headphones are always ready to go when I need them. The sound quality is exceptional. The audio is crisp, clear, and well-balanced across all frequencies. Whether I'm listening to music, watching movies, or taking calls, the headphones deliver a fantastic auditory experience. Speaking of calls, the integration with my phone is seamless. Whenever I receive an important call, the headphones automatically pause whatever I'm watching on my other device, allowing me to pick up the call without missing a beat. The built-in microphone is another fantastic feature. It picks up my voice clearly, and I've had no complaints from anyone on the other end of the line about sound quality. Additionally, the headphones are incredibly user-friendly. Pairing them with multiple devices is straightforward, and switching between them is smooth and hassle-free. The controls are intuitive, making it easy to adjust volume, skip tracks, and take calls with just a few button presses. In summary, these headphones offer outstanding quality at an unbeatable price. They excel in every area that matters—comfort, sound quality, battery life, and user-friendliness. If you're looking for a reliable, high-quality set of headphones that won't break the bank, look no further. I couldn't be happier with my purchase and wholeheartedly recommend these to anyone in the market for new headphones.

reviews.text: It's QuietComfort. For that, I'm gonna avoid critiquing the sound quality directly. Don't get me wrong, these sound amazing, but I have multiple over ear headphones that I use for different listening purposes. Still, I use these daily at my computer for multiple reasons, including work, and the ANC and comfort levels are what need to deliver for this price point. For instance, a quick example, the landscapers are coming through and mowing the neighborhood as I write this. With the ANC active, you wouldn't even know it. I mentioned wearing these daily, and for the most part, it's about 3-4 hours before a 1 hour break, and then another 3-4 hours. The synthetic leather ear pads won't do. In my opinion, they should never be used on headphones geared toward comfort, and I'm never gonna understand why they are. What's the point of a "long battery life" if these headphones get hot and sweaty after limited use? If your ANC is as good as it appears to be, I'll gladly trade some sound isolation with velour or cloth for more comfort, but with real leather, you wouldn't have to. Also, there isn't a PU/synthetic leather out there that doesn't inevitably break down and fall apart in the most annoying way possible. For $350+, I shouldn't have to limit sessions because I'm hoping to postpone that. My only other gripe is I have been unable to connect this pair of headphones to the Bose app across multiple mobile devices. I'm fine with my out-of-the-box experience with Windows, but this is unacceptable. Troubleshooting hasn't helped, and for now, I've given up accessing this device through the official app. To end on a high note, I've used these for some gaming sessions, and am quite impressed with the sound quality in some of my favorite single player titles. I wouldn't use these for online play. Not for quality reasons, but I know there are options out there better geared for that. Overall, these QuietComfort headphones don't justify the price. The synthetic leather coupled with the mobile app being completely useless has made for a frustrating time rather than a completely bad one. The ANC is the saving grace here as you should expect from this series, but as someone who has no experience with Bose's first generation QuietComfort headphones, it's kind of scary to think this is the 2nd generation. High end product manufacturers have this new bad habit of spoon feeding consumers "improvements" from one model to the next while somehow finding it in themselves to charge a small fortune in the process. I do like a lot about these, but the frustrations have limited some of the possible versatility here, and I'm stuck using these like any other pair of ANC equipped headphones on one platform. I'm hoping to get the app working. I'm liking the ANC and the newly discovered appeal these have doing some casual gaming while listening to some tunes, but this is an easy score to make for my experience.

products.description: What types of noise does ANC reduce best? ANC works best on steady background noise such as engines, road hum, AC, and fans. Voices and sudden sounds change quickly, so they may still be partly audible. ANC reduces these distractions rather than eliminating them completely How can I get the best ANC performance? For a smooth connection, make sure the headphones are charged and in pairing mode. If reconnecting, disconnect other paired devices nearby, forget the previous Bluetooth record, then pair again. A factory reset can be used if needed. How does Multipoint Connection work? Pair with the first device, turn its Bluetooth off, then pair DB QuietFocus with the second device. Turn Bluetooth back on and reconnect the headphones on the first device. They can now stay connected to both devices; audio plays from one at a time. How can I get the longest battery life? Up to 120H of playtime is achievable under specific test conditions. Actual battery life varies with volume, ANC, calls, and listening mode. reviews.text: These Beats headphones are really nice looking in person. The Cloud Pink color is soft and attractive, and I love the rose-gold accents because they give the headphones a stylish, premium appearance without being too flashy. They are very lightweight, which makes a big difference when wearing them for an extended period of time. The ear cushions are soft and comfortable, and the adjustable headband makes it easy to get a good fit. I also like that the ear cups fold in, which makes them much easier to store or take along when traveling. The sound quality is excellent for everyday listening. The audio is clear and balanced, with enough bass to make music enjoyable without completely overpowering the vocals or other parts of the song. I also love the spatial audio, which makes music and videos feel more immersive and gives the sound a wider, more engaging quality. They work well for watching videos, and the Bluetooth connection has been convenient with my devices. They are also compatible with Apple devices, making it easy to connect them with my iPhone, iPad, or Mac. The battery life is another big plus. Having up to 50 hours of playback means I don't have to constantly remember to charge them, and the Fast Fuel feature is especially useful when I realize the battery is getting low and need to use them quickly. Overall, these are a great pair of wireless headphones if you want something that sounds good, feels comfortable, and looks beautiful. I especially like the lightweight design and the soft pink color. They feel like a quality product, and considering the sound, spatial audio, battery life, comfort, Apple compatibility, and overall design, I think these are definitely worth the price.

globalReviews.text: The Beats Solo 4 represents a major technical leap for one of the most recognizable pairs of headphones on the planet. While the iconic, foldable design remains familiar, the internal hardware has been completely overhauled to meet modern standards. The Gold and Black aesthetic provides a high-end, sophisticated look that feels more mature than earlier iterations. One of the most impressive upgrades is the staggering 50 hours of battery life, which allows most people to go an entire week without reaching for a charging cable. Even if you do run out of power, the Fast Fuel feature provides five hours of playback from just a ten-minute charge, and the addition of a 3.5mm port means you can still listen to music even when the battery is completely dead. Sound quality has also seen a significant refinement. These headphones now feature custom 40mm transducers designed to reduce electronic interference and distortion, resulting in a much cleaner and more balanced sound profile than the bass-heavy Beats of the past. They also support Personalized Spatial Audio with dynamic head tracking, which creates an immersive, theater-like experience for movies and music. It is worth noting that these are "on-ear" headphones, meaning they rest directly on your ears rather than surrounding them. While the new UltraPlush cushions are incredibly soft, they prioritize a secure fit that stays put during movement, which some users may find a bit snug during very long listening sessions. Compatibility is another area where the Solo 4 shines, offering a truly "platform-agnostic" experience. They feature one-touch pairing for both Apple and Android devices and integrate perfectly with both "Find My" and "Find My Device" ecosystems. Unlike the larger Studio Pro model, the Solo 4 relies on passive noise isolation rather than active noise cancellation; while the thick cushions do a great job of blocking out office chatter and street noise, they won't completely silence a loud airplane engine. For the commuter or student who wants a mix of legendary style, massive battery life, and high-fidelity sound in a portable package, the Solo 4 is a top-tier contender.
globalReviews.title: Iconic style, modern performance

reviews.text: I bought these because I needed something that would allow me to enjoy music, pod casts and many other videos without being tied to my desk computer or iPhone. One main reason is I needed something that sounded good but nothing overly priced like my AirPods Pro that only get about 2 hours of listening. These are rated for up to 50 hours. And the best part was the fact they were inexpensive connect to more than one bluetooth device (my M4 Mac mini and my iPhone 14) in addition I needed something to be able to have a conversation if my phone rings while I am on my Mac. and these have worked so far flawlessly. Set up was a bit more then I expected I figured connect via bluetooth and off I would go but no, I did have to download the app to fine-tune the Headphones which wasn't a big deal. While they are not of the highest quality they are perfect for me and my listening needs. Incoming calls were a breeze and everyone I spoke to so far while wearing them had no issues hearing me. Now, I am a bit amphrehensive about the battery life because at the whole day yesterday of wearing them the battery monitor on my Mac claim the headphones were still 100%. and if that is true then they are even better than I was expecting battery wise. I did recharge them over night because I wasn't sure if the Mac was telling me the truth. The voice interaction with my phone calls were very clear and I have no complaints. The fit is really nice if you ask me and they are very light weight, after wearing them almost all day I would forget they were on and have to take em off. They are very comfortable to wear and I noticed just how light they were when I pulled them off and carried them over to where I plugged them in to re-charge. Of course it's only been a couple of days so, if I can edit this review at a later time I will do so, if there is a need to. I mean after only a few days these are brand new so I do need to give them more time. Surprisingly, my ears have not began to sweat with them being on all day, although. I do have issues with my ears being itchy from time to time but that's not because of the headset. That's just my ears. For the price the quality for me is really good. I may listen to a song or two but, I mainly wanted something to last longer than 2 hours if I watch YouTube or other streaming videos on my computer or iPhone. As well, they release my nice wired set that I used, I got tired of tripping over the wire and my office chair rolling over the cord and getting tangled up. Plus the added convenience of being able to get up from my desk and walk around my Apartment when I need to while I am listening to something is what I was aiming for. The quality again for me is really good, I am not a sound engineer so I could not tell you where on the spectrum of sound they fit but for the price to me they do the job I expect of them. All around a good pair of headphones for the price. Battery life may not be up to 50 hours because the battery monitor remained at 100% even though I had them on almost all day. But, they certainly lasted well past the 2 - 5 hours of wearing them compared to a pair of Apple AirPod Pros. I still want to kick myself for buying the Apple ones not realizing for the price they didn't last very long on a single charge. I highly recommend.

reviews.text: I've been using these every single day for the past four months, and I honestly can't believe how good they are for the price!! The battery life is absolutely INSANE. One full charge lasts me almost an entire month, even with daily use. I keep expecting the battery to die, and it just...doesn't!?! The noise cancellation isn't 100%, but I'd say it's around 70%, which is more than enough for me. It does a great job cutting out background noise so I can focus, and the sound quality is fantastic for $30 price range. Comfortable fit, I use for music, podcasts, and movies which all sound clear and balanced. Easy connectivity too with bluetooth on my TV and Apple products. If you're looking for an affordable headset with that classic over-ear look, amazing battery life, and really solid sound quality, I can't recommend these enough. I'm genuinely blown away by how well they've held up!

reviews.text: If you spend a lot of time on virtual meetings or listening to long audio formats, the Sony WH-CH520 headphones are a fantastic, budget-friendly choice. I use these primarily for Microsoft Teams meetings and listening to podcasts, and they perform beautifully. The built-in microphone captures crisp, clear vocals without picking up a ton of distracting background noise, which is exactly what you want for work calls. Audio playback is sharp and balanced, making spoken-word audio very easy to focus on. A few standout features: Insane Battery Life: They offer up to 50 hours of battery life on a single charge. You can literally go a couple of weeks of heavy daily use without ever plugging them in. Multipoint Connection: You can pair them to two Bluetooth devices simultaneously. I have them connected to both my laptop and phone, and they seamlessly switch over when a call comes in. Lightweight Comfort: The on-ear design is lightweight and well-padded, so they don't give you that heavy, clamped feeling during long marathon meetings. If you need a reliable workhorse headset for daily productivity, calls, and audio tracking, you really can't beat these for the price. Highly recommended!

reviews.text: My wife and I both got matching pairs (mine is tan hers is pink), and so far we are loving it. Great sound quality and I can talk on the phone with them as well (which I’m not used to). It’s also her first personal pair of headphones she’s ever had which she was (and still is) excited for. The battery life is great and it’s compact for easy storage. My only reason for not giving them 5 is that the headphones aren’t too comfortable in that they make your ears sore after long periods of having them on (due to not going over your ears but instead on them). Also because of the compact build it’s a bit difficult to rest them around your neck (but very comfortable to just have them on the head behind the ears). I’d say it’s still well worth the price and a great buy despite that (also love the colors).

reviews.text: The product arrived well packaged. There was a delivery delay but it was not horrendous and to be expected given that it was ordered during Parime Days, The headphones arrived almost fully charged, Set up was relatively easy, but you really do need to use their app to complete the set up process. The app also allows you to change some settings and select equalizer settings that work for you. The switches have a nice feel to them. They do have raised areas designed to help you find the correct switch by feel. There are times however when I find that it is easier to adjust the volume using the phone or I remove the headphone to make a change. This is a very subjective items so you may not have the same issue. No stars were deducted for that reason. These are an on ear device. It was not uncomfortable to me, but it did take some getting used to and here again...Personal preference comes into play. On a warm and humid day you may experience some sweating where the ear cup rides on your ear. That may allow for some movement / shifting of the headphone depending on what you are doing. They may thus not work out well for use doing exercising as an example. The sound quality is great at this price point. I have Bose ear buds. The sound from this device is not Bose quality and you should not expect it to be Bose quality. It is good to very good however. The equalizer settings allow you to control all five typical equalizer settings PLUS a separate adjustment for th4 bass. Paring was easy and fast. The connection remains stable most of the time. There is a selection that allows you to select either top quality sound or a more stable connection. I chose sound quality an the vast majority of the time the connection was stable with no noise present. There may be times however, that due to local conditions / interference you may have a little popping or very brief drop out. I have worn these headphones a LOT since they arrived and while I have experienced that, it was very limited. Now I also have a lot of electric / electronic devices in use on my property and that will may explain what I experienced. I did have some interference from some household devices when I wass very close to them. The battery life seems to be very good. I have worn m for several hours and the voice system still indicates 100% at startup. Unlike my Bose products the battery monitoring system is not linear where it will call out 100%, 90%, 80%b etc... It may call out 100% until the battery hits 50% (As an example) and then te voice system will drop from stating 100% to 50%. I do not see that as an issue or negative given the very long stated by the manufacturer battery life, and I have no disagreement with their claims about battery life aty this point in time, So again...Thus far I am very pleased with the fit, quality, and sound quality of these headphones. Do bed aware that tey are NOT noise cancelling. There will be some outside noise reduction dur to the ear cups of course.

reviews.text: This review is for the 520. I am the owner of the 500 also. So this review will be mentioning the 500 as a comparison. I got this product because I felt like the sound quality on the 500 which I bought several years ago didn't quite seem like it was as good as it used to be Of course I'm sure my hearing isn't as good as it used to be as well. I bought these because they were very affordable I mean how often do you find a product like this on sale This is Sony product that appears to have a high rating for reviews and it's between 30 and 40 bucks so not too shabby in that regard. Now of course if these are off sale they're probably more expensive and then you'd have to decide what you want to do personally if these were 50 or $60 I never would have bought them or if I bought them to try out I would probably return them. I'm only keeping them because the sale price made them such a good deal. The sound quality is actually a little better than my old 500 model and by that I mean it sounds louder at 50% then my 500 model does There's a noticeable difference so I would think definitely my old pair is probably just wearing out. That being said the old pair actually seems like better quality I don't know how to explain it It's the plastic it's the way it's formed something about it feels like a more expensive item than the one I have now. The 520 just seems like a cheaper lesser expensive plastic which may or may not be true I don't understand the manufacturing of course but it just has that feel to it. The only thing I got was it was the headset itself and a tiny charging cord which is sufficient I suppose It would have been nice to have a case or even some sort of bag to put it in. Other than that it connects to all my devices just like the old version did You works with everything I have flawlessly I love the mic feature I've used it to make a phone call while sitting in the backyard which my old model has as well and I asked a person I was talking to what they what the sound quality was like on their end they said it sounded fine. reviews.text: I have spent years fighting to find a decent pair of bluetooth headphones since no phone manufacturer wants to make a decent phone with a jack anymore (which is endlessly stupid, but I digress). I have tried everything form fancy expensive Galaxy Buds to a myriad of budget options, and all have the same problems. Flawed connectivity, noticeably glitchy, slightly reduced sound quality. These finally fix it. The inclusion of an option to use a headphone jack on devices that let you is a great feature. Along with multipoint connect. They fit perfectly around my skinny neck (your mileage may very on that), so travel with them is a breeze. And for the sound quality, these are absolutely the best headphones for your money. I was loathe to go to overears full time because I like being able to take one out to hear my surroundings, and every noise passthrough I used before was sucky. (usually the outside noise obnoxiously trebley). Not with these. I actually go to concerts to listen with my headphones on because it actually makes the concerts sound better than with no headphones. Extremely convincing, near perfect noise passthrough. The app is easy to use and has a great selection of features: from custom EQs, to adjusting the noise pass through, to other various quality of life settings. The 3D adaptive sound feature is great, though a little tricky to set up at first, and noise cancellation is very good, though not the best in the world. The battery life is also almost unbelievable. I use these headphones a lot--sometimes all day--and I still only have to charge them once or twice a week. Multipoint connection is also a very nice plus if, say, I am working at my computer and still want to be able to answer phone calls hands-free. There are some minor flaws with them, though. First sometimes very low bassey notes from the outside world can trigger the speakers in them and give you very loud, deep popping noises. (E.g., this occasionally happens when I am riding in the car and hitting bumps in the road). Occasional outside sounds in passthrough through will sound muddled. Also the noise cancellation--while quite good--isn't perfect for every situation. Specifically, it has more trouble than, say, Bose headphones with loud, sudden sounds like fireworks. But for the money, it is still the best noise cancellation and passthrough system you can buy. Another (minor) complaint, though, is that the adaptive settings aren't always very great. It often thinks I am sitting and automatically turns on noise cancellation when I am very much driving or walking around town or once even ice skating--all situations where passthrough is crucial. And even if I am sitting, sometimes I really want passthrough on (like if I'm in a cafe), but it automatically tries to turn noise cancelling on annoyingly. Thankfully, it can be easily overridden in the app. These days, I usually just keep the adaptive sound setting off and adjust the settings to fit the situation but sometimes it will randomly go back to automatic/adaptive mode. My final and complaint is with the microphone for phone calls. Sometimes it works perfectly and the other line can hear my fine, sometimes all they can hear is background noise, sometimes they really can't hear me at all. I am not sure if it is some sort of firmware issue or if the microphone placement is just too far from my mouth, but for phone calls it can be a tad unreliable. When it works, which is around 75% of the time, it's perfectly good even though I have to talk a little louder than I normally would sometimes. But all those flaws aside, these are probably the best all-around headphones I have owned and for the $120 I paid for them it's a steal. They may be more expensive as I got them on sale, but I have used headphones multiple times the price that are poorer quality and less functional than these. I'd have paid upwards of twice the price for what I got.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on May 22, 2023
reviews.title: Best Headphones I Ever Owned, Especially for the Money

reviews.text: Great sound quality and noise cancellation. These headphones deliver above their price point. The ear-cups are large enough to fit my ears inside so there is no pressure on the ears’ frame. This point is important for long wear with comfort during online meetings or prolonged use, like a long flight. The battery life is exceptionally strong and you can go all day, and longer, without the need to recharge. It can deliver up to 35 hours of battery life with Active Noise Canceling (ANC) turned on, and up to 50 hours with ANC turned off. The only reason I took away one star is the portability. The headphones do not fold and they don’t come with a case for protection. So Sony left it to the consumer who plans to use them outside home to manage how to protect the headphones. I luckily have a case that fit which I had bought for the previous model. Overall, I recommend these headphones and it’s a nice addition to my collection of Sony, Bose, Beats, Apple, and Sennheiser. Yes! I love headphones.

reviews.text: I can honestly say that these headphones are worth the investment. There are times when I still need to plug in my headphones with a 3.5mm cable, so I like that I can use them wired or wirelessly. When it comes to using them wirelessly with Bluetooth, they are amazing. You can connect the headphones to a single dedicated device or to two devices simultaneously. For me, that is such a great feature. I use the headphones to connect to my computer for work purposes, but they're also connected to my phone as well. The sound quality is the best I've ever gotten from a set of headphones. I've never experienced noise-cancelling audio as precise as this. And for the times when you don't need to totally cancel everything out, the ambient sound mode provides audio that is just as good. The Sony Sound Connect app you use with these headphones is designed to deliver the best possible sound. The equalizer function lets you control how you experience whatever you're listening to, offering options like bright, relaxed, vocal, speech, and bass boost. I use these headphones all day while I work, and they hold a consistent charge. I still have plenty of battery life left at the end of the day, but I usually plug them up to charge when I'm done with them. The volume control buttons on the headphones are easy to use. The only thing that can be frustrating at times is that the button to stop/start a song or move to the next track is right in the middle of the volume buttons, so I end up hitting it when I want to raise the volume. However, it is nice that they've also included a button on the headphones to toggle between noise-cancellation and ambient sound. Again, I use these for work, so I wear them for the majority of the day. They fit well and are comfortable to wear. As the day wears on, my ears do get a little warm from the cushions around the headset, but compared to how much I like using the headphones, it's a minor issue. The only other item of note is that, given the investment, it would be nice to include a storage box or bag. If you're on the fence about buying these headphones, I highly recommend them. They are worth the investment, and you'll be pleased with both the sound and design.

reviews.title: Exceptional Headphones That Are Worth The Investment

reviews.text: Update 3/9……so first I’m going to say that I bought these with my own money before any reviews were out. Didn’t realize they were a vine product. After a few weeks of use the padding has relaxed enough so that I can feel the drivers poking my ears. I wear my headphones around 4 hours a day on weekdays and 8-10 hours on each weekend day. As stated earlier I have a smaller than average head, and my ears do not stick out. I can usually adjust the cups to be lower, but I don’t like them riding my jawbone. I would’ve have overlooked that because they do sound good, however they are now randomly disconnecting. I use them for YouTube and I’m literally 18 inches away and they disconnect. I check through the app and it shows a connection failure. If I pause a video, again, they show connected, but the sound comes out of my iPad. When I check the app it tells me there is a connection failure and to restart. While the sound is good I don’t think I care to restart my headphones every 10 minutes. Maybe they don’t like Apple devices? I’m not sure…. I originally bought the xm5’s. I finally got them last week only to find they were quite oversized for my smaller than average head. The weight of them made matters worse as every time I looked down they flopped forward. I had to return them. I am not one of those fancy audio people but I know what I like. My previous headphone were the solo pro 3’s and I do enjoy them. What I don’t like is the pain my ears experience after about an hour of having them on. I wanted over the ear headphones and everything I read and all the videos I watched pointed me to the xm5’s which ended sadly. I searched Amazon and saw these were a new model. Looked up what little I could find online about them and the consensus was these were the cheap version of the xm5’s. Yeah, I’m sold so I got them. Build: They are cheaper feeling, not as bad as the 510’s, but nowhere near the xm5’s workmanship. But they are also not breaking the bank (as bad anyways, it still shocks me to see what headphones are going for nowadays). The sliding part is plastic reinforced by metal. I’ll be honest….I am wondering how they will hold up. Comfort: Excellent. These are super light. I don’t feel them resting on the crown of my head at all. There is no clamping on or around my ears. But the are secure on my head. The padding around the ear cups is decent and the cups are deep so most will not have their ears touching the speakers. Bells and whistles: these are old school, they have buttons…no swipe features at all. I like that because in my week of using the xm5’s I discovered quickly that volume adjustment was hit or miss with response time. It might be that my hands are always cold, but in 6 hours of wearing these I have already mastered the buttons. They are very well placed and very responsive. App: They are part of the Sony Headphone app. You get an equalizer and other customizable features including the ability to connect to two devices at the same time and it works great as I use the headphones for watching music videos on YouTube and Netflix. I use my phone to adjust the equalizer for the music playing on my iPad. Another feature on the app is you can set the headphones to shut off when not in use. I was excited about the auto shutoff feature. Not so much now. It is not sensor based nor is it based on when you device’s screen shuts down. It is based on when you turn of Bluetooth. This makes it worthless to me and maybe a lot of us who do not ever turn Bluetooth off. I think it could have been done better. Noise cancelling: I’m going to call this adequate. With my Beats Solo pro with ANC I can’t hear anything. Not even someone yelling. These will drown out the hum of a fan pretty well, but they let in a lot of ambient noise (like my husband coughing in the next room right now!). Even the xm5’s were not as good as the Beats. But the on ear style of the Beats may have something to do with that. So I’ll stick to the xm5’s comparison. I also want to say that there are supposedly 3 modes…noise cancelling, ambient and off. I have not noticed any difference between ambient and noise cancelling. There is no voice prompt to let you know which setting you are in. I will play some more to see if I’m missing a setting in the app and if something changes I’ll edit my review. Sound quality: (of course this is subjective to each person) Excellent out of the box and I could not say that about the xm5’s. My first mission was to find the equalizer when I took them out of the box and tried them. Not so with these. The sound was nice. I still tweaked it but if I wasn’t able to change it a bit, I would still be happy. Other: They do not come with a case. They do not fold. They come with an aux cord and charging cable, no charging block. Final thoughts: This is my fourth pair of headphones in a month. I was willing to drop over 300 bucks on a pair. And I didn’t like any of them. Most important to me is fit and sound. Most were severely lacking in sound quality. These are not. And they were cheaper. I am most disappointed in the build quality. I think they should’ve done better. To me $150 is alot of money to spend on headphones that feel this plasticy. And if they crack after 6 months I’ll be upset. I’m not expecting $350 quality, but better. These are not too much better than the 510’s when they should’ve been a little less than the 910’s. They are far less quality than the 910’s. Maybe I’m asking too much after coming from the Solo 3 pros and xm5’s which both have a superb build. BUT…..they make up for it in having great sound that you can totally adjust to your liking. They are comparable to the xm5’s in sound. And far superior I feel to the 910’s which just sound overly undefined bass. And the comfort!! It’s spot on. These are the best out there in terms of sound and app capabilities.

I’ve tried other headphones before, but their heavy weight always caused discomfort — this one never does, which is why I bought it. The sound quality is excellent, especially when tuned through the app: strong bass, clear vocals, and great clarity for editing and all types of music. I definitely recommend it. Just handle it with care because the plastic material can break if not used cautiously.
