globalReviews.text: Calidad / precio - Buen sonido, la app de Sony tiene varias configuraciones que ayudan a encontrar el ajuste perfecto. - Cancelación de ruido bien, no esperes que el ruido desaparezca un 100% yo diria que entre el sonido que aísla de manera pasiva + la cancelación de ruido incluida, el ruido se puede reducir un 70% - 80% segun el volumen del ruido y de la musica que tengas puesta, lo cual me parece suficiente. - Materiales, son muy ligeros, lo que pudiera dar la sensación de "fragiles", personalmente me parece mejor que no sean muy pesados a que se sientan muy macizos y eso le agregue peso. - App, como mencione, es muy buena y configurable, pensando en que estamos hablando de una app para audifonos, me parece bastante bien. - Precio, siempre es subjetivo, cuanto estas dispuesto a pagar? yo venia usando unos JBL de $800 aprox, estos Sony duplican ese valor pero considero que lo vale completamente y en todos los aspectos son mejores que mis anteriores audífonos, que de por si me parecen bastante buenos. Conclusion. Buenos audífonos para escuchar musica, peliculas, podcast, jugar etc.. tienen una cancelacion de ruido buena sin llegar a ser un 10 ni un 1, precio justo, materiales de construccion ligeros sin ser malos y una app bastante util.
globalReviews.title: Audifonos con calidad y precio justo

globalReviews.text: Lemme explain stuff in paragraphs Coming from Boat Rockerz 551 ANC btw, and I'm going to base my review around the fact that I used to be a Boat Headphones user. Also, point to be mentioned, I got these for around Rs. 5800 (yes, I got lucky with the discounts 😂) 1. The sound quality: I'd say it's a pretty big leap, around 50-80% better sounding (depending on the type of music I'm listening to). The bass is good just like the Boat headphones, but unlike the boat headphones, these have better quality bass, like, the Sony doesn't create a stinging/uncomfortable feeling in bass heavy songs. Also unlike Boat Headphone, Sony do give care to mids and highs. Do not get distracted by the fact that the Sony headphone's driver size is 30 mm (compared to Boat's 40 mm). Driver quality also matters, and in this case, it matters more than the size of the drivers. 2. Battery life: 100 hours (Boat headphones) v/s 35 hours (Sony headphones)? Well, there's no comparison, but 35 hours isn't too low either. Good enough, especially when you consider the fact that weight of the Sony Headphones is much lighter than Boat Headphones. 3. Active Noise Cancellation: Well, this one is a mixed opinion. I expected Sony to have around 50% stronger ANC, but, it was quite similar (maybe slightly stronger? I'm not fully sure) to my Boat headphones. Not disappointed though, the quality of ANC (ie, the ANC algorithms) is much better on the Sony. What I mean to say is that you get a weird feeling of higher air pressure in the enclosed ear area (especially in the eardrums) when you turn on ANC on the Boat, but that doesn't seem to be the case on Sony. Not to mean that the anc is bad, if you listen to music at 20% volume and have anc turned on, then the fan sounds will disappear, which is good. 4. Durability: Though both are made of plastic, Sony has at least given some care to the headband area (by reinforcing it with metal). My Boat headphones literally broke within 4 months of use, forcing me to use Epoxy glue to make a temporary fix and use them till I saved up enough to buy this Sony headphone. 5. Comfort: These are comfortable to wear. Good cushioning. Not much pressure on the ears. Can wear for long durations without fatigue. 6. Mic quality: Well, everyone I talked to while wearing the Sony weren't able to distinguish whether I was using a Headphone's mic or my smartphone's mic. It's good and clear (they were able to notice slightly worse mic quality on the boat headphones though). 7. Latency: Don't buy if you want to do hardcore competitive gaming. And even if you do, use it in wired mode or else latency will be quite high and noticeable (I'm guessing around 400 ms latency) 8. Bluetooth connectivity Both had good connectivity. No issues from that side. No random disconnects or something else throughout my use until now. Multipoint connectivity works well. 9. App integration Really good feature. You can tune it to exactly how you want it to sound as long as you know what you're doing. If not, then here's my suggestion: play your fav music, scroll through the presets available, and select the one which suits you the best. Well, these are the points I wanted to highlight. Good headphones to choose at this price range. Final verdict: Good purchase for those who want really good audio quality, decently good ANC and the Sony brand sound optimisations. UPDATE: So, it's been 338 days since I wrote the review, time to update it now (date of update: September 3, 2026) Rant alert, if you want the review update about the product strictly, skip over the following paragraph: Firstly, I'd like to thank all those who liked my review. Did not expect it to blow up this much, ended up being one of the top liked review in India (seriously did not expect that 😂). During this time period, I switched away from Boat fully (trust once broken can never be repaired). Used to have Boat Immortal 141 earbuds before, switched to Realme Buds Air8 now (bought it at around Rs.3100), hence I will base the review of it as well, just like how I did with the Boat 551 ANC in the initial review. Some might think "Why do I have 2 different audio products??", to that, my answer is that I am the sort of person who uses both on the regular basis. Earbuds in college (basically, for when I need portability), headphones in hostel (when I need max comfort for multi-hour continious use). So, starting with the review update about the product, I will keep it in the same order as before, same numbering and stuff, for the reader's ease: NOTE/CAUTION: I do not know what the current competitors offer at the same price range, hence the review update will be solely based on my experience with the audio gear that I own personally. 1. Sound quality: Still really good, doesn't dissapoint at all. Just the best for the price at which I bought it. 2. Battery Life: Still gives me 5-6 (sometimes 7) days of usage on a full charge, and mind you, I use it for at least 3 hours, with about 4-5 hours on weekdays on average, and about 7-8 hours on weekends (sometimes more, sometimes less). Hence, as I mentioned, still good enough, not as insane as the Realme Buds Air8's total battery life (case + earbuds) or the old headphones I compared with, but still respectable for my use. 3. Active Noise Cancellation: Honestly, after trying Realme Buds Air8, I would say it's weak, as those earbuds do some serious noise cancellation. But considering the fact that it trades multi-hour usage comfort to achieve that, I would still choose the Sony Headphones everytime when in hostel. But when it comes to travelling on the train, I will choose the earbuds even for long usage hours. So basically, if you want best ANC and don't care about comfort, then just go get a pair of earbuds, you'll be way more satisfied with that than this. 4. Durability: Didn't dissappoint (at least not yet, hopefully doesn't for at least another 4-5 years). Yes, they could have used something other than plastic, but it's fine according to me. Regarding the earcup status, I have attached few images. Those are taken on the day of me writing this update. Honestly, still holding up good, no damage at all, even after one wash to remove sweat (more on that later in the next point). Hopefully the earcups lasts me for another 1.5 years at least. 5. Comfort: These are still very comfortable to wear, like seriously, trust me when I say that I can use these for 6 hours straight and not feel uncomfortable. But fair warning: If you live in a place where it's humid, then you will sweat inside the earcups area (after long usage) and will have to take them off for a while and let the area around the ears dry (or wipe them dry). I myself faced this issue, and the earcups started smelling sweaty, so had to wash them with Ezee once, after which the smell went away. Also, pro tip: dust/particles/random-debris might collect inside the earcup area, please check inside and clean it on a regular basis, otherwise it will bounce around when you wear the headphone, into your ears and such, causing itching/irritation (yes, I am talking from experience on this one 🥀). WARNING: DO NOT DIP THE ENTIRE HEADPHONE INSIDE EZEE WASH SOLUTION (I seriously hope no one had this insane idea, but I shall add this anyyways). Remove just the earcups and wash those, do not wring it like how one does with clothes, be extremely gentle with it. Please research about it more if you plan on doing it. Do not do it randomly. Do not use a really strong concentration of ezee liquid (ie, a lot of it in very little water). Do it at your own risk. 6. Mic Quality: I would like to change the review from before on this one. Don't get me wrong, the mics are good, the audio that the other person hears is good and sounds like your real voice (and not the robot like voice), but in achieving that, the background noise also passes through to the other person. Ie, if you stand under the fan while talking to another person through phone call with the headphones on, he/she will be able to hear the sound of wind. I'd say that the Chinese audio products of the recent time nail the right spot on this one, like, when talking to someone on call with my Realme Buds Air8, the other person doesn't hear robot like voice, but the backgound noise seepage is also significantly lesser than the Sony Headphones. 7. Latency: Nothing to update, the thing I said before still stands. 8. Bluetooth connectivity: Nothing to update, the thing I said before still stands. 9. App integration: Recieved one software update for the headphones during this use period, didn't feel any difference, but yeah, still supported well ig. Nothing else to add. Final verdict: Still good to buy if you can get around Rs.6000, otherwise not really value for money. Definately don't go for it if it's above Rs.7000-7500, I think you will find some other better newer option at that price range. If you have any other doubts, then you might check my Amazon profile bio.

reviews.text: This isn't a paid ad for this company. I've had these headphones for about 4 years now and I'm finally deciding to leave a review. I bought these to replace some Bose inside the ear headphones that I stepped on and broke. Those were pretty good, but I didn't want to spend over $100 on a new set. I read the reviews on these and the reviews were pretty good. Plus these are inexpensive. I've bought my daughter and wife a pair of Beats for $200+. They both love theirs so I decided last night to compare my KVIDIO to my wife's Beats, and I was seriously and embarrassingly blown away. I was embarrassed because I spent so much on the Beats and the sound quality isn't even close. And I am very serious about this! the KVIDIO headphones gives good highs and a good solid bass. I can hear the music the way it was intended to be heard. With the Beats, it was just louder but there was no depth as if the levels were turned all the way up. With KVIDIO, the levels seemed to be fine tuned for the music I like to listen to. The battery seems to last for several days without needing to be recharged. The noise cancellation works very well. I use them when I'm mowing the lawn, and they drown out the loud mower motor. I also use them when I'm talking on the phone. I've never had anyone complain that they couldn't hear me, and I've always been able to hear the person clearly. As a matter of fact, if I get a call, I will put them on hold until I can get my headphones. But, that isn't really about the quality but more about me not wanting to hold the phone in my hands. They are still my go-to. Again, I waited 4 years to write a review and I am no shill. I was just so surprised at the quality of these compared to others that were 10x the price! I would buy these again and recommend to anyone.

reviews.text: These sound excellent for the price. Not "audiophile grade", but that's nowhere near expected for $30. The value is ridiculous. Comfortable, lightweight, fits well without falling off or exerting painful pressure on the head over prolonged use. Battery life is VERY impressive, though I tend to listen at low to moderate volumes, which of course will extend the time between charges. The soft materials feel great, though I can't speak for longtime longevity of the pad covering for example, since I haven't had them for years. Overall, the sound profile is way more balanced than I would expect from a budget headphone. It genuinely sounds fairly accurate with surprising clarity. No frequency range feels too recessed, nor is it too in-your-face. Keep in mind, these aren't crystal clear, silky smooth, or perfectly even across the full frequency range, but those are characteristics reserved for a WAY higher price point and are completely unexpected here. - Bass reproduction is imperfect, not totally even, has some undesirable resonance in lower frequencies that can muddy the experience, but it's less of an issue than I'd expect at this price point. It's not way too overtuned, but it's also not anemic or lacking. Also, repositioning these on the head slightly can help with the muddiness. I'm pretty sure there's not a $30 headphone under the sun that actually has great bass reproduction, so definitely not knocking a star off for this. Worlds better than a lot of bass-boosted consumer headphones, without falling into the insipid tin can category. - Mids are pleasant and generally sit in the right spot in the mix. If you don't crank them up, they're not too harsh or "serrated-edged", but not buttery smooth either. More than acceptable, but can sound a little shouty at times. They will get harsher at louder volumes. - Highs aren't crystal clear, but don't feel too lacking or unnaturally excited. They won't present perfectly in a busy mix, but once again, nothing will at such a price. It's impressive how they're always serviceable, never totally getting lost or garbled while also not being painfully piercing. - Soundstage is just okay, but absolutely good enough for a super-affordable closed-back headphone. Like everything else, it's better at a moderate volume where things feel less compressed in general. They get really loud (too loud) from a regular source like a phone, whether over Bluetooth or a wired connection. The best sound quality will definitely come at a moderate volume though, since the drivers don't begin to present that "overmic'd" sound with a harsher edge as most do speakers and phones do closer to their volume limit, and separation will be better when they're not struggling. One of my biggest pet peeves—at least on my phone—is that every time they connect after turning them on, they default to the same volume, which is WAY too loud for me and can actually hurt my ears and leave me with an hour or two of discomfort and slightly reduced hearing acuity. Make sure to turn them on, begin playing your media and double-check your volume levels before putting them on your head to avoid this. I take pride in my sensitive hearing and this is very important. It's also worth mentioning that the volume control on the headphones themselves is awkward since it requires holding a skip button. This means it's hard to make a delicate adjustment, since you have to hold it long enough to change at all, but not so long that it adjusts too far up or down. I recommend finding the setting that sounds the best, then adjusting on your device from that point forward. Overall, these are a no-brainer if you want $30 over-ear bluetooth headphones with solid, accurate-but-acceptably-compressed sound quality, great comfort, stellar battery life and a completely solid connection even from several yards away.

reviews.text: I got these because I don't like to have to solely rely on Bluetooth. When I'm laying in bed for the night I like to be able to plug them into my tablet and watch whatever I want while my husband sleeps peacefully. If I'm up listening to music or on the phone I will use the Bluetooth so I'm not tethered by a cord. They are easy to pair and comfortable to wear. I often fall asleep in them and they don't hurt my ears. I don't like earbuds for that particular reason. They cover my entire ear and the cushion on them is pretty thick, so even though they don't have noise cancellation I've still found them blocking out noise around me. The only thing I knew I wasn't going to like about them was the 3.5 mm aux cord. It didn't look very long and it also wasn't equipped with the option of a microphone so if I had to plug it in to talk on the phone I couldn't use the headphones. Let's say my battery died for the Bluetooth then I would be left with no options to plug them in to my phone and continue a conversation. That was an easy fix though and when I purchased the headphones at the same time I purchased another cord that had the dual 3.5 mm aux cord one on each side. This cord was also more sturdy as it had the braiding around it, giving me the ability to speak through the cord, pause what I am watching Plus turn my volume up and down on videos. The Bluetooth speaker is very clear and I have no issues with others hearing me or me hearing them. When I use the cord I purchased separately I also have no issues with hearing people or people hearing me. When I went looking for headphones, earbuds or anything that would give me this dual capability I was afraid that such a thing did not exist. I wasn't elated that I came across these headphones. They were exactly what I was looking for and the sound quality is perfect for me. I had a pair of Bluetooth AirPods but they weren't the ones with silicone tips. I hated them as they would fall out of my ears and it's so easy to lose one of the earbuds. I ended up giving them to my sister and bought these instead. I'm very happy I did and I'm glad I bought the extra cord along with it from a different vendor on Amazon. Just finding earbuds that fit in my ear are constant struggle. I end up having to buy the ones that wrap around your ear because my ear holes are just too small even with the smaller silicone tips. I also have another pair of wired earbuds that wrap around my ears that I bought off Amazon and I keep them as a backup. If something happened to these headphones I would 10 out of 10 buy them again. I don't care about name brands and never have when it comes to these sorts of things. Most of the time when you buy name brand you're just paying for a logo. A very long time ago probably around 2010 I asked my ex who runs a computer business what flat screen TV to buy that would last me the longest. He told me to get a Vizio TV. I had never heard of that name but I trusted him. Here we are all these years later and my Vizio has stood the test of time. I definitely recommend buying these headphones and if you have teens that are looking for something like this I'm sure they would love them. If they don't like the logo on the side you can always paint over it. They can even customize the headphones with their own design using paints or whatever. Just make sure they top it off with a clear coat. The only thing you can't do is charge them and use them at the same time. You have to let them charge then you can use them from there. I have zero complaints 💜✨ Edit: I'm now 6 months in and still love these headphones. Even sleeping in them hasn't caused the cushioning to flatten or crack. So happy I gave these a chance and didn't spend tons of money on a brand name. These have truly exceeded my expectations. I'm not afraid that they will get lost or broken because if they unfortunately do even though I would be sad I could just buy another pair without breaking the bank. Still in love with them 💜 1 yr 4 months and still going strong!!!! Love these headphones!!! 💜💜

globalReviews.text: I love these headphones! I have purchased these headphones 3 times. I'm thinking of getting another pair. When I bought my first set, they were for my computer... for gaming and Discord (voice chat). I was tired of having wired headphones with that annoying cable running all over the place. Or worse, having to step away from the computer and forgetting you're wired to it and yanking the headphones off. I grabbed these because the price was right and honestly... I don't know what the difference between these and a $200 pair is. Read on to see why... The sound is good. Maybe not audiophile territory but I have no complaints. The Bass is bass-y... explosions sound awesome, car engines rumble nicely, I'm not going to get into all the sound effects, youll be reading all day, but suffice it to say... good sound. I bought a second pair for my phone and TV because I was so impressed with the quality of these headphones. That is how I found out they can connect to 2 devices at the same time! I'm not sure if that's common or not, but *I* was pleasantly surprised. When used for the TV, they definetely sound better than the TV speakers. For the phone they were good for phone calls, but where they excelled (for me) was when I listened to music. I have an eclectic taste in music but a few genres I listen to when I'm out and about are 80's, Techno, EDM, and some classic rock. These headphones managed to make it all sound great! Careful with the volume if you want to keep your hearing into your old age though, they can get LOUD. The third pair I bought was for a family member because I was so impressed with these. They use them for the PC and PS5. The best thing about these headphones, and the reason I'm looking into pair #4 is.... the battery life. OMG. I have used these things for over 12 hours straight... they were on and playing sound the entire time. Didn't need to charge them for the next day because, tbh, I forgot to plug them in... and they went for another 2 days before they reminded me to charge them. The second pair (for the TV / phone) I have charged, used for a couple hours, and left on the nightstand for DAYS before I used them again and they were fine. Didn't need to be charged. It's insane. I'm not sure when I bought the first pair, but it has to be around 2-3 years ago and they're still going strong. The faux leather covering on the speaker cuffs has long since worn away so that kinda sucks. Also, the depth of the cushion could be just a tad thicker beacuse, as time has gone by, the cushion has lost some cushion-y-ness and the ridge of my ear can make contact with the fabric covering the speaker. (I just bought pipe cleaers, twisted some together and then wrapped them around the inside of the cushion to "Red-Green" them. iykyk) I should note, that of the three I've purchased over the years, they are ALL still in use and working well.

reviews.text: I purchased these earbuds about a year ago. I use them 4 to 8 hours a day, at least 5 to 6 days a week, and they still work like new. I use them for my GPS, listening for orders in different Gig apps (spark, instacart, doordash, ubereats), and for phone calls. It isn't very often that I have to put them to charge throughout the day. If I do, usually on busier/ longer days, I put them in the case for maybe 10 minutes and they're ready to go for the rest of the day! Even after all this time/use they still charge quickly and hold a charge very well. If I listen to music, the battery does drain faster, so on those days I do have to charge them extra, but they still only need a few minutes in the charging case. The case holds a charge exceptionally well. I only have to charge the case every other day. This pair of earbuds has held up to me dropping them more times than I can count. I am really hard on them and they are really standing the test of time! I have very small ears and even small earbuds hurt my ears or just won't stay in them, but not these. They stay in my ear well most days and are so comfortable I forget that I am wearing them. I live in the deep south with horrible heat and humidity, and on those days the earbuds can sometimes work their way out of my ear, but that would happen with any earbuds while sweating in a triple degree heat index! I mean, it is hot enough to make your ears sweat! Lol My son borrows them occasionally and the larger rubber earpieces fit perfectly for him. They're really easy to pop the rubber ear piece off and clean with alcohol wipes. While the sound quality isn't top of the line, it's pretty great for how little these cost! I am soft spoken and have had issues in the past with callers hearing me with other Bluetooth, but I haven't had that issue with these. I can hear callers well, as well as them hearing me well. I keep the earbuds set to "ambient aware" and can hear everything going on around me as well as whatever is playing through the earbuds. I don't like spending a lot of money on earbuds because I have broken/ lost so many!! (dropped in: bucket of mop water, airplane toilet, the gap walking into the elevator, trash chute, and a storm drain). So instead of getting a high end Bluetooth that cost more, I was trying to find the best earbuds I could for as low a price as I could find. I tried these since the price was so low. I figured if I have to replace them at least I'm not paying too much, but instead, I found a pair of earbuds I love! And I love the pretty ballerina pink!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 5, 2026
reviews.title: Great earbuds at a great price!

reviews.text: Just upgraded from the original JBL Vibe Beams to the Vibe Beam 2, you instantly notice the difference. The bass is punchier and the overall sound is a lot crisper and more detailed. One of the best upgrades for me is being able to switch between ANC and Ambient Aware right on the earbuds without having to open the app. You do have to tweak this in the app first and make a choice between keeping the volume adjustment on the left bud or having the choice to swap ANC for Ambient Aware or Talk Thru but for me not having volume adjustment is not that big of a deal. The ANC does a solid job filtering out background noise. When I’m sitting next to the TV, the chatter gets cut down nicely while at the same time sharper sounds still come through clearly to the point where I can still hear the conversation im having even with music playing at medium to high volume. Everything feels detailed and well-balanced. Really happy with these, JBL did not disappoint. If you already liked the original Beams, the 2s feel like a proper upgrade in both sound and a good bang for your buck. In size, they're similar to the previous, the new white color makes them feel more appealing and fresh. The Quick Connect is also a very neat feature to not have to scramble through bluetooth to reconnect. And if you multitask, the multiple device connect is neat, up to 2 devices can be connected and switch in between for example my phone and pc. I will update on the battery life as soon as I give them a good run.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on September 4, 2026
reviews.title: Big improvement to the previous Vibe Beams

reviews.text: These earbuds work great with my iPhones 13 and 17. They paired easily (remove them from the case) and the sound is good to my non-technical ears. Using the free JBL phone app, the functions of each bud can be changed to your preference, and they also connect with Siri and take phone calls although I've not used those two features yet. I have the left one controlling volume and the right one controlling play/pause and forward/back. You can choose the noise cancelling controls instead of one of those if you want. You can also change the sound and other things in the phone app. The app adds a lot of options. The buds are comfortable in my ears. They work less well with my Fire tablet, although they do work. It took several tries to get them to pair and the sound doesn't seem quite as good, but this Fire tablet is quirkier than a previous Fire I had. Also, the magnets in the case seem strong and the buds are sometimes a little difficult to grasp and remove from the case, but that's a minor thing. I've only had them a couple of days with no problems so far. I walked down my driveway to my mailbox at the road with them paired to my iPhone in the house and they did not drop the sound, so the range seems good. These replace a pair of more expensive Beats Studio buds that apparently sat in a drawer too long. I can't get those to charge now and I need a pair for an upcoming trip. AI says the battery in those is probably gone. The cases are a similar size and appearance. No complaints with these JBL buds so far and they seem to be a better value.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on June 23, 2026
reviews.title: Working great!

reviews.text: Just got these, and for the price they’re not bad. The noise canceling option is decent, but not amazing. I like that I can adjust sounds through the app and they feel comfortable on my ears and not feeling like they’ll fall. There were some connectivity issues, but only as I was getting them set up and the sound quality is decent as well, though some things sounded louder than others. They battery life seems very good, I charged once and used all day (pausing many times) and the battery only went about 5%. Giving 4 stars only because the sound could be crisper and smoother, but for the price, they get the job done.

reviews.text: Not impressed. I purchased this set https://a.co/d/09jpLM2h and have used them daily for over a year. I like them so much I bought the black and white versions. I decided to get an ,"upgrade" for my birthday and purchased this JBL set, as I'm kind of a JBL fanboy. While the sound is marginally better, everything else about them is not. The $20 no name set is more intuitive, has more control options, and a better case. Cheap buds lower volume and rewind/previous song from the left bud, volume up and fast forward on the right bud. JBLa have NO VOLUME control, and all seek pause functions are controlled by just the right bud. The left bud operates the AI and non-existent noise cancelling. They don't even feel as nice as the cheaper set. Not having volume control is very frustrating. The cheaper buds have a better feel to them, like an actual touch screen. The JBLs feel like a pen. Not as pleasant. The case is worse too. The cheap one has a digital display that shows how much charge the case has. The JBL just has a single led that shows green, yellow or red. What do those colors mean? No idea. They even store oddly. The $20 ones ear easier to remove from the case too. And lastly the $20 set lasts between 30 minutes to an hour longer than the JBLs. Other than the tiny difference in audio quality, the ones that cost half as much are many times better in functionality. I am truly disappointed. **Edited July 13th, 2026. I had the left earbud in while taking a shower. It got wet, and now the volume doesn't work. Returned as defective.**

reviews.title: These are not the buds you're looking for. (returned)

reviews.text: I have had experience with JBL products in the past, and from those experiences, I was expecting a much better richer Boulder sound. I was expecting more customizable options in regards to base, death, and better sound quality. Other than that, there’s not much else that I can say about it except for I was really hoping the sound was a lot richer a lot Fuller and the noise canseling a lot more than it is. The other thing that I have noticed is that when you are in a vehicle and you are going over potholes and bumps in the road, it gets a lot of static in the headphones while you are listening to music. That is something I noticed since I use public transportation a lot it interrupts the sound quality while going over different cracks or potholes in the road. Overall, the product is good, but it does need to work in those areas at least in my opinion.

reviews.text: It's been a few months since I bought these and they were a serious disappointment. Let me start by saying that my previous JBL earbuds were near-perfect for years. One finally stopped taking a charge so I bought these Vibe Beam 2 versions. They fit a little loose even with the larger ear tips. Most importantly, the sound quality was just plain bad. The bass was simply not there – it was like listening to an AM radio station. My older JBL's would practically vibrate your entire skull, especially if you gave them a little extra push into your ear to seat them better every once in a while. These new earbuds had the microphone extensions while my older ones did not. Yet my callers told me there was no difference in sound quality. If that's the case, I'd rather have them less obtrusive. Speaking of case, this new one was fine and charged pretty fast. As for the price, it's a blessing and possibly a curse. The price is very good and affordable. But you get what you pay for no matter how many shiny words are in the description. I paid double for my old JBL earbuds and that was during a Christmas sale at a local warehouse club store. If you don't want a lot of bass and have small ear cavities, these may be great for you. As for me, I'm going to try to find a new pair of my old set.

globalReviews.text: Ces écouteurs font vite ce qu’on attend d’eux : ils chargent rapidement, offrent une autonomie durable et tiennent bien dans les oreilles. Le design est confortable et pratique pour tous les jours (travail, balades, vidéos). 🎧 Ce que j’ai remarqué Charge rapide et batterie qui tient bien la durée Construction solide, pas fragile du tout Son correct pour le prix, même si ce n’est pas du niveau “haut de gamme” audiophile 🔊 Il y a aussi ce que je pense être un mode transparence (ou réduction passive du bruit) qui laisse passer les sons de l’environnement lorsque tu n’écoutes rien — ce qui est pratique pour rester conscient de ce qui se passe autour. Je n’ai pas encore testé si ça fonctionne pareil avec de la musique, mais sans musique c’est notable. ✅ En résumé : Très bons écouteurs quotidiens pour appels, vidéos et musique casual Charge rapide et autonomie fiable Pas de son premium, mais efficaces et confortables Je recommande si tu veux une paire pratique et durable sans vider ton porte-monnaie.
